title: Combined envelope/balanced axes and geometric flags: conditional κ = 5.1778825456819e-5
body:
## Conditional result

Combining Dominik Scholz’s PR #76 h23 axis, Chafik Boukhalfa’s PR #79 h25 axis, and our PR #78 geometric coordinate flags gives

$$ T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=\frac{51778825456819}{10^{18}}=5.1778825456819\times10^{-5}. $$

This is **0.06415998% above #79** and **0.077600% above #76**, under all inherited all-size and analytic hypotheses. Bit saving is `51781506642569/10^18`. Both complete parent child lists are strictly excluded at the new saving using their own widths.

**Full verification completed.** All expanded `make verify` groups are covered by the recorded original and resumed runs, followed by the new focused checks (82 isolated test modules; 7 new controls). The first run stopped at a local Apple Clang OpenMP configuration error; the failed group and every remaining group passed after enabling installed libomp. No checks were bypassed. Receipt: `research/combined-flags/validation.json`. All 42 GitHub checks passed on the validated research/packaging head; this follow-up commit only adds the receipt. No unconditional theorem, global optimality or practical speedup is claimed.

## Combination

Each axis implements the same full triple-indexed map and dirty-role interface. We select the complete #76 h23 implementation and #79 h25 implementation, preserving every endpoint, copied center, data term and complex cost. We then permute coordinates consistently across frames, source triples, outputs and scatter rows. Permutations commute with I+J and preserve the bilinear form, so interfaces and full data-case histograms remain valid. Internal corner profiles are rebuilt from the actual changed words.

| Quantity | Combined witness |
|---|---:|
| h23 roles | 27,256 |
| h25 roles | 35,684 |
| W | 134,031,764 |
| Total recursive rank | 77,066,417,400 |
| Rank deficit | 1,846,900 |

Axis selection without geometric relabeling gives κ = `51767625345147/10^18`; the coordinate search supplies the remaining improvement. Thus reported percentage gains are not simply added together. The width bridge is derived afresh: 27 wire bits, row coefficient 843, degree gap 7007/25.

## Checked

- Both relabeled words regenerate byte-for-byte from pinned parent words.
- Independent full ordinary-input and arbitrary-dirty-basis replay in both orientations.
- Complete physical transition reconstruction; exact bounded-minor/CRT profiles with zero disagreements.
- Complete paid cost/rank identity, independent rational moment bounds, 47 strict inequalities, seven margins, and adjacent bit/κ grid rejection.
- Seven focused tests cover six physical/coordinate mutations and three stale bridge fields.
- Dedicated Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 CI; all inherited workflows retained.

Run `python3 research/combined-flags/verify.py`, then `(cd research/combined-flags && python3 -m unittest test_controls -v)`, plus `make verify` for the expanded inherited suite. See `research/combined-flags/README.md` for the general combination/relabeling argument and `SOURCE.json` for provenance.

The branch inherits #79’s portable source package. #76’s original scheduling package and supplied witnesses are archived unmodified with licenses. Its original compiler regeneration still requires its documented immutable #71 archive; our verifier directly replays the pinned word and does not require that archive. Regenerating our relabeling is not a claim that #76’s original search/compiler was portably regenerated.
